title: 2012 AMC 10B Problem 17
statement: Jesse cuts a circular paper disk of radius \(12\) along two radii to form two sectors, the smaller having a central angle of \(120\) degrees. He makes two circular cones, using each sector to form the lateral surface of a cone. What is the ratio of the volume of the smaller cone to that of the larger?

solutions.text:
Each sector forms a cone with slant height \(12\). The smaller sector has angle \(120^\circ\), so its arc length is \(\dfrac13\cdot2\pi\cdot12=8\pi\), giving base radius \(4\). Its cone height is \(\sqrt{12^2-4^2}=8\sqrt2\).

The larger sector has arc length \(16\pi\), giving base radius \(8\). Its cone height is \(\sqrt{12^2-8^2}=4\sqrt5\).

The volume ratio is \[\dfrac{\frac13\pi\cdot4^2\cdot8\sqrt2}{\frac13\pi\cdot8^2\cdot4\sqrt5}=\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{10}.\]

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: The sector arc length becomes the base circumference of the cone
